options.help: The game's own console profile. Series S is its low preset (smaller textures, lower detail, 1080p); Series X its high one (2160p).
options.cost: Series S is about 2-3x faster than Series X

options.help: The screen size the game is told the console is plugged into (WxH, 640x360 to 7680x4320). Measured on the Series X profile: the game renders its scene at 2560x1440 whatever this says; the setting sets the size of its final picture (and drops the 3840x2160 colour, depth and upscale targets when it is smaller: about 0.5 GB of card memory). On a 1440p monitor 2560x1440 is native.
options.cost: Series X: only the final plane and about 0.5 GB of memory change (the scene stays 1440p); the Series S console option lowers the scene's size

options.help: Which graphics card to use on a PC with more than one: part of its name (5060) or #index. Empty: Windows' default card.
options.cost: Pick the strongest card

options.help: Shrinks the game's window to at most WxH (keeps aspect, centred). The picture is stretched: softer, same frame rate. Not a render-resolution setting.
options.cost: None

options.help: Game-side: the fraction of the output height the game renders at before its own upscaler (0.2 to 1.0; the hook cannot go above native).
options.cost: Lower is much faster and softer

options.help: Game-side: forces the game's own temporal upscaler on (the console profile Series S needs it at any scale below 1).
options.cost: Small cost, hides the lower render scale

options.help: Which screen the game's window opens on: part of the monitor's name (Alienware), DISPLAY1, #index (0 is the first output) or primary. Empty: the primary screen. The log lists every screen at start.
options.cost: None

options.help: A borderless window the size of the chosen screen instead of a small window (the picture is stretched to it).
options.cost: A bigger window costs a little GPU time

options.help: auto: HDR output when Windows HDR is on for the chosen screen (turn on Use HDR for it in Windows Settings; VIctory never changes that). on: always tell the game HDR is available and present PQ/BT.2020. off: SDR. stretch: APPROXIMATION, the game stays SDR and its picture is expanded to HDR.
options.cost: None

options.help: HDR only: the brightness in nits of SDR white (the interface, menus and the numbers panel; default 200). The game's own HDR picture is not changed by it.
options.cost: None

options.help: miss: rays end at the root (no traced shadows or bounced light; the stand-in light below fills in). off: as miss, and the ~1,034 ray-tracing resolve and traced-shadow shaders are skipped (fastest). cpu: the title's ray-tracing structures are built on the CPU (XboxBvhBuilder replaced) and the rays are walked for real: traced shadows, bounced light, reflections; EXPERIMENTAL.
options.cost: off is fastest; cpu costs CPU time for every build and GPU time for every ray

options.help: Rays end at the root (miss) while the structure builder is off. Off: the title's ray walks run and may hang on stale structures.
options.cost: On is faster and avoids hangs; off needs the structure builder (not available on NVIDIA)

options.help: list: skip the ~1,034 ray-tracing resolve and traced-shadow shaders of scripts/rt_off_hashes.txt (diagnostics build only). none: run them.
options.cost: list saves GPU time; the skipped passes give less bounced light

options.help: Stand-in for the indirect light the rays would give: this share of an estimate worked out from the frame (0 or off: the title's own, black indoors). Also constant:<level>.
options.cost: Almost free (one small compute pass)

options.help: Bound for the light the air scatters, as a multiple of the light around (0: the title's own). Lower removes brown fog veils indoors.
options.cost: Free

options.help: How many times the estimate the title's own light may keep (4 when unset). Lower stops rooms by a window from glowing.
options.cost: Free

options.help: Crease shading of the stand-in: <strength>,<radius in metres> (default 1,0.6).
options.cost: Free

options.help: Stand-in light: the title's own light that is strongly magenta (green under half of red and blue) is taken as stale probe memory and replaced by the estimate (Vice-Tay 1bf62e1 / Belobug 81ebb7bd). On by default (0: off). Needs the ambient stand-in on; read at start.
options.cost: Free; also drops real magenta light (neon) the title wrote

options.help: A NaN a shader writes is made 0 before blur and upscaler spread it: removes black blobs. Baked into translated shaders.
options.cost: Tiny cost

options.help: Texture residency policy: auto = the new budgeted policy (floor, reserve, eviction); legacy = the base's rule.
options.cost: auto keeps more detail resident within the card's budget

options.help: Hard cap on host texture copies in MB (legacy residency only). Empty: derived from the card's budget.
options.cost: Higher is sharper but risks spilling card memory into PC RAM (stutter)

options.help: Top mips of a host copy bigger than this are dropped (0: none; empty: the build's default: 8-64 MB by card at 7c0cdf6, off at 28d8475 because a cap banded the picture). Higher keeps more close-up detail.
options.cost: Higher costs video memory (and can spill into PC RAM on small cards); lower fits small cards

options.help: With levels-on-demand textures (VICTORY_LEVELS_ON_DEMAND=1) on a full card: the smallest levels of a texture get tiles anyway, up to this many MB in all, so it shows blurred instead of black until its large levels fit (0: off).
options.cost: Costs up to this much card memory; large levels still wait for room

options.help: Lets go of the host copy of a placed texture at once when the title remaps its memory (instead of after the idle time), when nothing shows it.
options.cost: Frees card memory sooner; a copy still needed is made again (upload)

options.help: What is done when a DirectStorage write or a finished plain read lands bytes under placed textures. default: open the guarded blocks. textures: also make the placed textures under it due again, plain reads too (fxceless e4245f3; for black or garbled faces in the opening cutscene). all: everything. slots: slots only. off: count only.
options.cost: textures re-uploads textures that were uploaded before their data landed

options.help: Host copies go back to the COMMON state after a placed copy (VIctory-RTX 50347f8), so a later copy or shader read never finds COPY_DEST.
options.cost: Free (a barrier per placed copy)

options.help: Memory the residency policy keeps free for everything else.
options.cost: Higher is safer, textures get less room

options.help: Texture bytes always admitted whatever the memory use.
options.cost: Higher keeps more detail under pressure

options.help: Texture MB staged to the card per frame under the new policy (automatic: 48-192 MB by card).
options.cost: Higher fills textures faster, longer frames

options.help: Texture MB uploaded per frame (empty: automatic). Higher drains the first minutes of black surfaces sooner.
options.cost: Higher: faster fill, hitchier frames

options.help: Whether texture refreshes wait for the title's memory to hold still. wait: correct skin/materials; no-wait: faster, can show rainbow skin.
options.cost: no-wait saves about 7 fps

options.help: Upload textures ahead of the draw lists that use them (less pop-in).
options.cost: Slightly less hitching

options.help: Retired host objects are dropped by a helper thread instead of the thread that lands flights (playablegames-peppa 92b7cf9).
options.cost: Not measured on this machine: may save a few ms of that thread's time

options.help: Landed lists are reset by a helper thread after a submission instead of the submitting thread (playablegames-peppa cb41295).
options.cost: Not measured on this machine: may save 2-4 ms of the submitting thread

options.help: Relay stage for the title's copies. 1: correct bodies (no stretched or jumping characters); 2: faster.
options.cost: Stage 1 costs about 7 fps with card steps 0

options.help: Card-side steps of the relay. 0: correct bodies; 2: fastest.
options.cost: 0 costs the submitting thread about 30 ms a frame

options.help: Milliseconds a frame may wait for new shader pipelines to compile instead of skipping their draws (default 500). Higher: fewer missing objects, longer first-time hitches.
options.cost: Only costs time the first time a place is seen

options.help: Descriptor slots for dynamic views. Too few drops draws (missing objects) on cards capped at 1,000,000.
options.cost: None

options.help: Video memory for card-side copies of the title's buffers (memory compares on the card, not the CPU: about 2x fps on Series S). Measured on an RTX 3080 with the smallest size below at 64: 2048 holds all copies (about 1.9 GB made).
options.cost: Larger is faster until memory runs out

options.help: The smallest title buffer (KiB) that gets a copy in the card's memory; smaller ones are read by the shaders across the PCIe bus. Measured (RTX 3080, 1440p, 5,000 draws): 64 instead of 1024 cut the GPU's command time from 82 to 48 ms a frame and the frame from 135 to 110 ms, for about 540 MB of card memory. 4, 16 and 64 measured the same. Overrides the MB setting of the same name.
options.cost: Costs about 0.5 GB of card memory; saves about 30 ms of GPU time a frame

options.help: Zero-copy memory on integrated or unified-memory GPUs.
options.cost: Faster only on shared-memory hardware

options.help: Legacy residency only: the share of card memory textures may fill (default 90).
options.cost: Higher keeps more textures, risks spilling into PC RAM

options.help: keep: idle texture copies stay up to 10 minutes while memory is free; release-early: dropped after 5 s.
options.cost: release-early saves memory, causes re-uploads

options.help: Seconds a copy of title memory (a "window") that nothing holds may go unused before it is freed (0: only the free-RAM rule, five minutes with plenty of RAM). Frees PC memory only (these copies are shared memory, not the card's); a window the game comes back to is copied again.
options.cost: Frees about 1 GB of PC memory in a long run; a re-copy of 4 MB per window the game returns to

options.help: Copies of textures are made level by level on demand (needs tiled-resources tier 2). Saves memory.
options.cost: Saves memory, small CPU cost

options.help: Threads that map the title's memory (empty: 8).
options.cost: More can help streaming, costs CPU

options.help: Threads that compile shader pipelines (empty: two thirds of the cores).
options.cost: More shortens first-time hitches, takes CPU from the game

options.help: Keep the ~1,000 ray-tracing resolve shaders instead of leaving them out while the structure builder is off.
options.cost: Costs GPU time; the light they give is wrong without structures

options.help: EXPERIMENTAL: builds the ray-tracing structures. Cannot run on NVIDIA cards (64-lane programs refused).
options.cost: Large cost; may hang

options.help: Mouse and keyboard as a gamepad: the mouse is the right stick (the cursor is hidden and held at the window's centre while the game is in front), keys per bindings.ini. Unset with scripted keys (VICTORY_KEYS*): off.
options.cost: None

options.help: Path of a bindings file (copy bindings.ini and edit: Sensitivity, key per button). Empty: the built-in profile.
options.cost: None

options.help: A real GameInput mouse device the game polls itself (cursor motion inside the window, three buttons; vnvidia 12b1d16). The cursor is put back to the window's centre when it leaves the middle half, so a sweep does not stop at the edge.
options.cost: None

options.help: device: the mouse is the GameInput mouse above. stick: the mouse look is the right stick of the keyboard's stand-in pad instead (ItsMK1's way; the game then has no mouse device).
options.cost: None

options.help: Exact half-float rounding in translated shaders. Baked into shaders: the first run re-translates everything.
options.cost: Extra instructions

options.help: Shows the numbers panel (F3 toggles). F8 opens the quality page whether or not this is on.
options.cost: About 50 microseconds a frame

options.help: Scoped timers and a stall report at the end of the run.
options.cost: A few percent

options.help: GPU timestamps per pass for the numbers panel and profile.
options.cost: A few percent
